stories.headline: Supreme Court orders new trial for Daniel Granillo
stories.summary: The Hawaiʻi Supreme Court ordered a new trial for Daniel Granillo after finding FBI hair and fiber testimony that overstated the science influenced the jury in his 1990 trial.
stories.text: The Hawaiʻi Supreme Court has ordered a new trial for Daniel Granillo, who has spent 36 Maui was sentenced to six years in prison after being convicted on Maui of kidnapping and sexual assault. Granillo's 1990 trial relied in part on FBI testimony claiming microscopic hair and fibers linked his car to the victim. But the FBI later acknowledged that its testimony overstated what the science could establish. The Supreme Court found that evidence did influence the jury and ordered a new trial. The original samples are no longer available and witness memories have faded, leading Granillo's attorney to say he doubts Maui prosecutors will retry the now 67-year-old who remains at Halawa Correctional Facility awaiting the next step.
